events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $7.26 (model confidence 0.88)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip — the fare is built from base, distance ($1.41/km) and time units, not a fixed quote [F6], so any extra detour mileage entered the rider's charge and RD-2's metered branch applies rather than the flat-fare branch.

RD-1 is engaged: the GPS track contains one off-route segment, 14:27–14:37, driving 6.47 km where the optimal route covers 1.32 km, adding 5.15 km and straying up to 1194 m from the optimal route [F3]. The driver's obligation is the shortest and most direct route absent reasonable cause, and no threshold applies to that duty [RD-1].

No exemption rescues that segment under RD-5. The driver's request was sent at 14:29 [F7] and the rider's "Sure, go ahead." at 14:30 [F8], both after the segment began at 14:27 [F3]. RD-5 requires the rider's agreement to be timestamped before the off-route segment starts, and a route named only after leaving the optimal route is not prior consent; the driver's later statement of prior notice [F9] is contradicted by the chat timestamps, and the system-side timeline/segment record governs [F3][F7][F8][RD-5].

No reasonable-cause exemption applies under RD-4. The only traffic evidence is speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on the Ayer Rajah Expressway and band 5 on Jurong Town Hall Road [F10][F11], neither of which is band 1 or 2, and band data alone does not exempt; no qualifying incident was recorded on the replaced stretch [F12]. The segment therefore stands as an unexempted detour [RD-4][RD-1].

RD-3 does not exempt it either: there was no rider-named stop on the route, and RD-3(b) concerns rider-requested stops, not a driver-proposed route the rider merely endorsed mid-segment [F3][F7][F8][RD-3].

RD-2 fixes the amount for RydeTAXI as the unexempted segment's extra kilometres at the trip's own per-km rate, distance_fare ÷ distance_km = $20.43 ÷ 14.5 km = $1.4099/km [F6]; 5.15 km × $1.4099/km = $7.26 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The residual between the total billed excess ($8.35 for 5.9 km [F4]) and the segment sum (5.15 km [F3]) is map-matching residue and is not refundable [F4][F3][RD-2]. No waiting component is refundable: waiting charged was $0.00 [F6][RD-2][RD-3].

RD-6's flag condition is not met: the driver's 90-day profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F15], so no prior upheld route deviation exists and this case cannot make the conduct "repeated" for flag purposes; profile facts could only support an additional action, never decide the case [F15][RD-6]. The rider's own dispute record [F14] likewise carries no weight on the merits.

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $7.26 Ryde voucher to the rider for the unexempted detour mileage (RydeTAXI metered trip, RD-2), and record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file for the 14:27–14:37 off-route segment. Do not add an account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip — the fare is built from base, distance ($1.41/km) and time units, not a fixed quote [F6], so any extra detour mileage entered the rider's charge and RD-2's metered branch applies rather than the flat-fare branch.

RD-1 is engaged: the GPS track contains one off-route segment, 14:27–14:37, driving 6.47 km where the optimal route covers 1.32 km, adding 5.15 km and straying up to 1194 m from the optimal route [F3]. The driver's obligation is the shortest and most direct route absent reasonable cause, and no threshold applies to that duty [RD-1].

No exemption rescues that segment under RD-5. The driver's request was sent at 14:29 [F7] and the rider's "Sure, go ahead." at 14:30 [F8], both after the segment began at 14:27 [F3]. RD-5 requires the rider's agreement to be timestamped before the off-route segment starts, and a route named only after leaving the optimal route is not prior consent; the driver's later statement of prior notice [F9] is contradicted by the chat timestamps, and the system-side timeline/segment record governs [F3][F7][F8][RD-5].

No reasonable-cause exemption applies under RD-4. The only traffic evidence is speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on the Ayer Rajah Expressway and band 5 on Jurong Town Hall Road [F10][F11], neither of which is band 1 or 2, and band data alone does not exempt; no qualifying incident was recorded on the replaced stretch [F12]. RD-2 fixes the amount for RydeTAXI as the unexempted segment's extra kilometres at the trip's own per-km rate, distance_fare ÷ distance_km = $20.43 ÷ 14.5 km = $1.4099/km [F6]; 5.15 km × $1.4099/km = $7.26 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The residual between the total billed excess ($8.35 for 5.9 km [F4]) and the segment sum (5.15 km [F3]) is map-matching residue and is not refundable [F4][F3][RD-2]. No waiting component is refundable: waiting charged was $0.00 [F6][RD-2][RD-3].

RD-6's flag condition is not met: the driver's 90-day profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F15], so no prior upheld route deviation exists and this case cannot make the conduct "repeated" for flag purposes; profile facts could only support an additional action, never decide the case [F15][RD-6]. The rider's own dispute record [F14] likewise carries no weight on the merits.

RIDER: We reviewed your dispute and are refunding you $7.26. The meter on your RydeTAXI trip is built from distance and time, so extra kilometres driven show up on your fare. Between 14:27 and 14:37 the trip went off the most direct route, adding 5.15 km that was not exempt: the driver's message about the new route came after that stretch had already started, so it does not count as your agreement beforehand, and the traffic readings for that stretch do not qualify for an exemption. We refund the extra kilometres at your trip's rate, weight, wait time was not charged. The $7.26 comes as a Ryde voucher on your account, normally, short while. Your account is not affected.

DRIVER: We reviewed a rider dispute about your RydeTAXI trip on the 14:27–14:37 stretch and found the detour was not exempt. Your message proposing the alternative route was sent after that stretch had already begun, so the rider's reply could not be agreement given in advance, and the traffic readings for that stretch do not meet the exemption conditions. This is a route deviation breach recorded on your driver file. No account flag is added, since we look at your recent record, not a single case, for that. Nothing is deducted from your earnings for this; the rider's $7.26 comes from Ryde as a voucher. Keep to the shortest direct route unless the rider agrees to a change before you leave it.

claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the driver added 5.9 km over the 8.6 km optimal route (+69%), including a single off-route segment from 14:27 to 14:37 that drove 6.47 km where the optimal route covers 1.32 km, adding 5.15 km and straying up to 1194 m from the optimal route.

Because this was a RydeTAXI metered trip, the extra distance was billed to the rider: the fare shows $8.35 excess distance (5.9 km × $1.41/km) on a total of $31.56, so the off-route mileage entered the rider's charge.

The rider's consent did not cover the off-route segment: the driver's request ('ok if I go round via West Coast Highway?') is timestamped 14:29 and the rider's 'Sure, go ahead.' at 14:30, both after the off-route segment began at 14:27, so there was no agreement before the deviation.

The driver's claimed justification of building traffic on the Ayer Rajah Expressway is not sufficient for the RD-4 exemption: the speed band recorded on AYE during 14:11–14:48 is band 4 (30–39 km/h), not band 1 or 2, and no traffic incident at all was recorded near the route in the trip window.

On the RD-2 metered formula the rider is owed the mileage on the unexempt off-route segment: 5.15 km × $1.41/km = $7.26, consistent with the fare record's $1.41 per km rate and $8.35 total excess-distance charge.

The driver's account history (one upheld dispute in 90 days) plus an upheld deviation here makes this conduct repeated, supporting a referral of the driver's account to Ryde review as an additional action; the profile data alone does not decide the deviation.

weaknesses: The chat record shows the rider did in fact agree to the West Coast Highway detour ('Sure, go ahead.', F8) and the driver's statement matches (F9); the driver will argue the whole route change should be exempt under RD-5 and will rely on the fact that the detour did avoid the slow AYE (band 4, F10).

Part of the deviation is not recoverable: the gap between the total billed excess ($8.35, F4) and the sum of the off-route segment (5.15 km, F3) is map-matching residue that RD-2 does not refund, and RD-2 also excludes any waiting component (waiting $0.00, F6).
The rider's own profile shows 2 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld (F14), which the driver may use to suggest a pattern of unfounded claims.

claims.assertion: The only off-route segment in the trip is 14:27–14:37, which added 5.15 km (F3); the rider's consent message was sent at 14:30, inside that segment rather than before it, so the segment is not consented to under RD-5.

The driver's justification for the reroute was building traffic, but the only traffic records are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on the Ayer Rajah Expressway and band 5 (40–49 km/h) on Jurong Town Hall Road (F10, F11), neither of which is band 1 or 2, and no traffic incident at all was recorded near the route (F12); the driver's own chat describes merely building traffic (F7), so no exemption under RD-4 applies and the segment counts as an unexempted detour under RD-1.

This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (F6 base/distance/time meter structure; distance billed at $1.41/km), so under RD-2 the refund is limited to the unexempted segment's extra kilometres at the per-km rate: 5.15 km × $1.41/km = $7.26, which is the part of the billed excess mileage ($8.35 for 5.9 km, F4) that corresponds to the detour (F3).

The remaining 0.75 km of billed excess distance (5.9 km actual excess minus the 5.15 km segment, F1 vs F3) is map-matching residual of ≤ 0.25 km class plus ordinary route slack and is not refundable under RD-2; no waiting fee was charged (F6 waiting $0.00), so there is no additional RD-3(c) refund.

The driver's written statement that he told the rider before going via West Coast Highway (F9) is contradicted by the timestamps in the chat log (F7 at 14:29, F8 at 14:30) falling inside the off-route segment (F3), and system timeline records prevail over the statement, so the driver gains no RD-5 exemption from it.

The driver's 90-day record shows 1 upheld dispute but none of them route-related (route: 0, F15), so the RD-6 threshold of a previously upheld route deviation is not met and no flag_account should be added on that basis.

weaknesses: The rider did in fact agree to the West Coast Highway route in writing (F8 'Sure, go ahead'), and the driver's statement (F9) supports prior notice; if the judge reads the 14:30 message as covering the whole segment rather than only its tail, RD-5 could exempt the segment and RD-2 would yield no_action — the deciding weakness for the rider is the 14:27 start of F3 versus the 14:30 timestamp.

The excess distance actually billed to the rider is $8.35 for 5.9 km (F4), larger than the $7.26 attributable to the segment; the rider will argue the full 5.9 km was caused by the reroute (F1), so the driver cannot avoid a refund entirely, only cap it.

The reroute did occur and was never explained by any incident record (F12), so RD-1 breach is recorded against the driver regardless of the amount; the driver has no traffic fact to rely on because F10 is only band 4, not band 1 or 2.

points.response: Agreed on the legal effect: the consent at 14:30 (F8) sits inside the off-route segment that began at 14:27 (F3), and the driver's request came at 14:29 (F7), so under RD-5 there was no consent before leaving the optimal route and the segment is unexempted.

Not contested: the only traffic records are band 4 on the AYE and band 5 on Jurong Town Hall Road with no incident near the route (F10, F11, F12), which is short of the band 1/2 or incident evidence RD-4 requires, so the segment stands as an unexempted detour under RD-1.
Agreed: this is a metered RydeTAXI fare ($1.41/km distance line in F6), so RD-2 refunds the unexempted segment's extra kilometres, 5.15 km × $1.41 = $7.26, which is the rider's requested amount.

Agreed that the 0.75 km gap between the billed 5.9 km excess (F1, F4) and the 5.15 km segment (F3) is map-matching residue outside RD-2, and that no waiting fee was charged (F6 waiting $0.00), so the rider does not press for more than $7.26.

Agreed: the driver's statement of prior notice (F9) is contradicted by the 14:29 request and 14:30 agreement (F7, F8) falling inside the 14:27–14:37 segment (F3), and system records prevail, so the driver gains no RD-5 exemption.

The rider withdraws the flag_account request: the driver's 90-day record shows 3 disputes with 1 upheld and it was not route-related (F15, route: 0), and RD-6 requires an already-upheld route deviation, so the additional action is not available; this does not affect the RD-2 refund of $7.26.

Conceded on the measurement: the track does show a single off-route segment 14:27–14:37 adding 5.15 km (F3), so a RD-1 breach to that extent is not contested; the driver only contests that the consented routing request was rider-initiated in effect and that the refund is capped by the metered formula.

Accepted that this is a RydeTAXI metered trip so extra mileage entered the fare (F6 metered distance $20.43 for 14.5 km at $1.41/km), but the billed excess of $8.35 covers 5.9 km (F4) while the unexempt segment is only 5.15 km (F3), so RD-2 limits the refundable mileage to the segment's extra_km and excludes the residual 0.75 km.

Conceded that the request (14:29) and the agreement (14:30) both post-date the segment start at 14:27 (F3, F7, F8), so RD-5's 'before you go' condition is not satisfied and the driver takes no exemption from the chat; the driver's contrary statement (F9) yields to the chat timestamps.

Conceded: AYE is recorded only at band 4 (30–39 km/h) and no incident was recorded near the route (F10, F12), which is below the band 1/2 threshold and lacking the (a)-type incident evidence RD-4 requires, so the reroute has no reasonable-cause exemption.
The arithmetic 5.15 km × $1.41/km = $7.26 matches my own computation from F3 and F6 and is the correct RD-2 cap, but only that segment mileage is refundable, not the full $8.35 billed excess.

Disputed: RD-6 requires a previously upheld route deviation in the last 90 days, and the driver's profile shows 3 disputes with 1 upheld but route: 0 (F15), so this case is not 'repeated' route deviation and no flag_account may attach; profile facts may never decide the case.

Withdrawn in part to avoid over-arguing: the driver does not press that the 0.75 km gap is a separate non-refundable residual beyond noting that RD-2 refunds only segment extra_km (F1, F3, F4); the rider's own history of 2 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld (F14) is not relied on as a finding.
